motion: Do conscious persons possess nonphysical mental substances that can survive bodily death?

burdens.description: Establish that conscious mental life includes nonphysical properties borne by a mental subject distinct from the organism or brain.
burdens.successCriteria: A reviewer can mark success only if an identified mental feature resists a physical identity or account and the argument connects that result to a distinct subject or substance.

burdens.description: Establish that the numerically identical conscious subject can persist or recur after the present body and brain cease functioning.
burdens.successCriteria: A reviewer can mark success only if bodily continuity is shown unnecessary for personal identity and a stated mechanism or probabilistic argument supports persistence or re-embodiment after bodily death.

burdens.description: Establish that persons and their mental states are states of natural organisms or brains without an additional mental substance.
burdens.successCriteria: A reviewer can mark success only if a naturalistic identity or scale account covers a central mental feature and leaves no indispensable explanatory role for a separate mental substance.

burdens.description: Defeat post-mortem personal survival by showing that consciousness and personal capacities depend on the functioning organism and brain.
burdens.successCriteria: A reviewer can mark success only if evidence links loss of relevant brain function to loss of the subject or its capacities and defeats an independent identity or recurrence route to survival.
